pages.text: Once, the world was whole.$(br2)Continents stretched beyond the horizon. Nations rose and fell. Civilizations flourished beneath an endless sky.$(br2)Until one day... the balance was broken.

The earth trembled. The ground split apart. Mountains crumbled, oceans swallowed the land, and the world as we knew it was torn to pieces.$(br2)Where continents once stood, only fragments remain - islands scattered across an endless abyss, suspended between the sky and the void.

Humanity vanished. Those who survived gathered together in the last remnants of civilization, clinging to a single hope: that this shattered world could still be called home.$(br2)But they were not alone.

From the depths beneath the broken earth, creatures emerged. Monsters unlike anything humanity had ever known crawled into the light, claiming the ruins of the old world as their own.$(br2)And one by one... the last remnants of mankind began to disappear.

Yet you are not afraid.$(br2)Where others see ruins, you see opportunity. Where others see dungeons, you see the foundations of something greater. And where others see the end of the world... you see a beginning.

Armed with the forgotten technology of the old age, you set out into the unknown. Airships will carry you across the shattered skies. Water will give you power. Steam will fuel your machines. And the wind will guide you toward lands untouched by mankind.
But this world will not rebuild itself.$(br2)You must explore it. You must tame it. You must defend it. And above all... you must rebuild it.

Gather the scattered survivors. Reclaim the forgotten lands. Build settlements among the ruins of the old world. Create something that can endure.$(br2)Because you may be the last one capable of doing what humanity itself could not.
Not merely surviving this broken world... but colonizing it.$(br2)A new age is waiting to be born. And its future... is in your hands.

$(l)YEAR 16 AFTER ZOMBIE$()$(br2)I do not know if anyone will ever read these pages. Perhaps that is why I am writing them down.$(br2)The world I once knew is gone. Where I once walked along the sea, there is now nothing but an endless abyss. The VOID.

Sixteen years have passed since the earth collapsed beneath our feet, and yet there are still mornings when I wake with the quiet hope that somehow, everything will be as it once was. The old cities. People. Machines. Voices. Anything.$(br2)But there is only the wind.

It sweeps between the shattered islands of the sky, whistling through the ruins and broken structures. Sometimes, when the wind grows strong enough, it sounds almost like the mournful groan of some enormous creature lurking deep within the abyss below.$(br2)I often wonder if something truly is down there. Something we cannot see. Something that was never meant to reach our world.

The monsters came soon after the Collapse. Creatures we once believed belonged only to the deepest parts of the mountains crawled from the ruins and into the light.$(br2)We had hoped the dead would remain exactly that.$(br2)Dead.$(br2)We were wrong.
They do not speak. They do not hesitate. They simply come. Every night, they wander out of the darkness and attack the last villages that remain. We have started calling them Zombies.

I killed one today. It was not difficult - these creatures are slow and seem to possess little intelligence. But when my sword pierced its chest, something happened.$(br2)A light burst from the wound. Not fire. Not magic. Something else.

It reminded me of something I once read in the old scriptures. A three-headed creature. A being spoken of in fragments and half-forgotten legends.$(br2)I never thought much of those stories before the Collapse. Now... I am beginning to wonder if we should have.

Earlier today, I spoke with one of the merchants who occasionally visits our tavern. He told me about a group of people who are attempting to summon that very creature. They believe it may be powerful enough to restore the world to what it once was.
According to him, all they need is a star. A star created through some ancient and questionable ritual. They believe that this strange star is the key to bringing the creature into our world.

I do not know whether I can trust the merchant's words. Perhaps he is simply trying to sell us another impossible dream.$(br2)But if there is even the slightest chance that he is telling the truth... then perhaps this is our only chance.

Our only chance to see the world as it once was. To see the sea again. To hear the cities. To know what it feels like to live without fear of what waits beyond the darkness.$(br2)Perhaps... we can bring our world back.
